binders: An arbitrary type Omega equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure mu on Omega, with an instance asserting that mu is a probability measure.
An arbitrary real-valued function X : Omega -> Real.
hypotheses: There is no separate measurability assumption on X at the outer level; measurability is built into every admissible scale and every right-side property.
On the right side the witness K is explicitly required to be positive, and each concrete property redundantly includes K > 0.
conclusions: The infimum over all finite nonzero extended-nonnegative scales t for which X is measurable and the integral of exp(|X|/t) is at most 2 is strictly below infinity if and only if at least one of four alternative conditions holds at some positive real scale K.

The four alternatives are: exponential tail decay P(|X| >= t) <= 2 exp(-t/K) for every t >= 0; real-moment growth integral |X|^p <= (Kp)^p for every real p >= 1; the interval exponential-moment bound integral exp(lambda|X|) <= exp(Klambda) for every 0 <= lambda <= 1/K; or the one-point bound integral exp(|X|/K) <= 2. Each alternative includes measurability and the relevant integrability requirements.
mathematical_definitions: The left-hand scale is sInf {t in ENNReal | X is measurable, t != 0, t != infinity, exp(|X|/t.toReal) is integrable, and integral exp(|X|/t.toReal) <= 2}.
For the tail alternative, probability is represented as the real conversion of mu({omega | |X omega| >= t}).
For the moment alternative, powers are real powers (rpow), p ranges over all real p >= 1, and the inequality is integral |X|^p <= (Kp)^p.
For the interval exponential-moment alternative, lambda ranges over all real values in [0,1/K].
The four-element index carries no numeric ordering; it merely selects one of the four properties.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On any probability space and for any real-valued function X, the exponential-integrability scale obtained by minimizing the positive finite t for which E exp(|X|/t) <= 2 is finite exactly when X satisfies at least one of four standard-looking exponential-tail, linear-moment-growth, interval exponential-moment, or one-point exponential-integrability conditions at some positive constant K, with the precise measurability and integrability clauses stated above.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The left side uses an ENNReal infimum. If there are no admissible scales, its complete-lattice empty-infimum behavior is relevant; the target compares that result with infinity rather than directly asserting existence of an admissible scale.
Admissible scales in D004 explicitly exclude both 0 and infinity before converting t to a real denominator.
The theorem does not assume X measurable globally, but both sides can hold only through definitions that require measurability; a nonmeasurable X yields no right-side property.
The right side asks for only one of the four alternatives, not all four, and the scale K may depend on the chosen property and on X and mu.
The outer 0 < K conjunct is redundant because every concrete alternative also contains K > 0.
The moment condition quantifies over real p >= 1 and uses real rpow, not merely integer moments.
The tail condition converts the measure from ENNReal to Real; on a probability measure this is finite, but the conversion is nonetheless part of the formal statement.
The interval exponential-moment condition includes lambda = 0 and lambda = 1/K and bounds by exp(K lambda), not by a fixed constant.
No centeredness or mean-zero condition is present, and every occurrence is based on |X|.
ambiguities: The anonymized four-constructor type provides constructor identities only through their recursor positions; the mapping to tail, moment, interval exponential-moment, and one-point conditions is inferred exactly from the displayed recursor order.

The dossier states the abstract complete-order implementation of sInf but does not restate the empty-set infimum law; its possible role is therefore identified as a boundary risk rather than assumed away.
